answer_text: YouTube is filled with videos addressing this exact question, and from my own experience, about 90% of them focus on exploring the idea rather than actually making money with it. In the hopes of cashing in on the trend, I launched a blog in the highly competitive AI niche. My motivation stemmed from hearing about people earning around $1000/month or roughly Rs. 83,000 using ChatGPT content. What I did was extract scripts from YouTube videos that garnered the most views on specific ChatGPT topics. I then transformed these scripts into articles with the assistance of ChatGPT. Unfortunately, the results weren't as promising as I expected. As you can see from the website graph, there was a small surge in impressions, but it quickly fizzled out. Despite creating 45 pieces of content since I started in April 2023, my website struggled to gain traction. When I reached out to the community for feedback, the response was that my website didn't comply with E.E.A.T guidelines. I acknowledge that I didn't include an author bio, as it was just an experiment, and I was testing my luck, which unfortunately didn't pan out. After a two-month hiatus, I decided to revive the project, but this time with a long-term approach, planning for at least 5 years. I'll gladly share the domain name once I see my website back on track in Google Search, likely around December 2024. Returning to your question, making money with ChatGPT is not as easy as it might seem. The chances of success, in my opinion, are around 5% or even lower. To illustrate, consider the Google Search Console graph of an e-commerce website I managed a couple of months ago. We incorporated human-written content, and even after ceasing new posts, Google continued to reward it with consistent traffic. For another perspective, look into the NBA Blast case study by Surfer SEO. Surfer SEO proudly uses AI content, but the website's traffic stats, as seen on SEMrush, reveal a rather stagnant situation. The key takeaway is that making money with ChatGPT requires more than just utilizing the tool¡ªit demands strategic planning and a lot of luck. If you possess the skills to develop an application using the ChatGPT API, such as a ChatBot tailored for a specific business, there might be potential. However, keep in mind that this could also require an initial investment to market your solution effectively. In essence, ChatGPT is a helpful tool, but turning it into a profitable venture is more a matter of luck than a guaranteed outcome. I hope my answer provides a realistic perspective.

question_title: (5) What have you learned from traveling abroad? - Quora
answer_text: One of the most eye-opening experiences I¡¯ve ever had was my first trip to Ukraine, a little over 20 years ago. I had visited France and Germany years before (as a child), but as soon as I landed in Ukraine, I quickly realized the rest of the world doesn¡¯t operate quite like the United States. The Soviet Union had collapsed about a decade earlier, but the country was still recovering¡ªand honestly, not much has improved since then. I could go on and on about the vast differences I noticed, but here are just a few things that stand out in my mind. First, everyone needs to use the bathroom several times a day, but public toilets were either nonexistent or left much to be desired. Some of them were what we¡¯d call ¡°chamber pots¡± in the West¡ªporcelain bowls¡ªwhile others were literally just holes in the ground, which you sometimes had to pay to use. I quickly learned to carry my own toilet paper everywhere because it was considered a luxury and wasn¡¯t available in most public restrooms (if you could call them that). As far as the toilets go, yes ¡ª they did have regular flush toilets in Soviet-era apartments. But from what I¡¯ve heard, a lot of homes in very rural areas may still rely on outhouses. The first time I saw a squat toilet or pit latrine, I was honestly shocked. I had never seen anything like that in my life, and it was extremely unpleasant. Needless to say, I didn¡¯t use too many of them ¡ª they were just too nasty. That said, some places did have nicer ones. I remember a church I visited in Kiev that had surprisingly clean facilities, and there were a few other spots that weren¡¯t too bad either. But overall, it was hit or miss, and most of the public toilets I came across were not something I was eager to use. What really surprised me even more was that people were expected to pay to use some of those¡ªeven the nasty ones (the pit latrines). There was also very little privacy in the bathrooms¡ªor latrines. From what I understand, many countries outside the Western world still use squat toilets. These include places like China, India, various African countries, and even Turkey. I¡¯ve also heard that Western European countries like France and Greece used to have them as well, but they¡¯ve largely been phased out in recent years. ***(By the way¡ªjust as an aside¡ªwe can all thank two Englishmen for inventing and improving the flushing toilet. The first was Sir John Harington, who came up with an early version of the flush toilet back in 1596. Then, centuries later, Thomas Crapper helped improve and popularize it during the Victorian era.)*** Not everything works smoothly in Ukraine, and it can take a long time to get things fixed¡ªlike the ¡°lift¡± (elevator) in apartment buildings. When I first visited, there were no lights in the hallways or stairwells. I remember my friend¡¯s mother met us outside during the day and had to use a flashlight to guide us upstairs. That felt so strange to me because in most American apartment buildings, the lights are usually working in the hallways and stairwells (I mean outside the apartments). And it was like this in ALL the apartment buildings I visited. I was told that the lights were cut off to save money. I guess it was considered an unnecessary expense and that people could live without it for a while. I was also told that the heat in Soviet-era apartment buildings was centrally controlled ¡ª meaning the entire building shared the same heating system, and residents couldn¡¯t turn it on or off themselves. The heat was only activated during certain months of the year, usually starting around October and shutting off in spring, no matter what the actual weather was like. So if it got cold early or stayed chilly later than usual, people just had to deal with it. As for air conditioning, that wasn¡¯t really a thing. Most apartments didn¡¯t have it, and people relied on open windows and fans during the summer. The whole setup was pretty different from what I¡¯m used to, where you control your own heat and A/C with a thermostat. There were no clothes dryers either ¡ª the apartments weren¡¯t built or wired for them. Everyone hung their laundry to dry, either on balcony lines, in bathrooms, on stairwells or in courtyards. And there was absolutely nothing handicapped accessible¡ªnot that I needed it, but I often wondered how people with disabilities managed to get by there. Just thinking about it was pretty depressing. When I asked some people about this they just shrugged their shoulders and I said ¡°I don¡¯t know. They just stay at home.¡± Seeing firsthand what life was really like in Ukraine made me appreciate the USA all the more. For those of you¡ªespecially my fellow Americans¡ªwho love to criticize the U.S., I encourage you to take a step back and reevaluate your perspective. You¡¯ve had it too good for too long. You don¡¯t even realize how good you have it. That being said, I truly enjoyed visiting Ukraine¡ªit was a fascinating and life-changing experience. And by ¡°life-changing,¡± I mean it opened my eyes to the reality that not all countries are like the United States. It made me realize just how good most Americans have it, and how often we take that for granted. Most of the Ukrainians I met were kind, hospitable, and incredibly resilient. After my first visit, I returned two more times, and with each trip, I saw signs of life gradually improving for many people. Sadly, with the war that¡¯s currently going on, it feels as if that progress has been stalled¡ªat least for now. ***And there¡¯s one more thing I want to add. I've noticed that a lot of people today seem to think life was terrible for most people decades ago¡ªeven during the 20th century. Many believe that things didn¡¯t really improve until the 1980s or later. But I don¡¯t fully agree with that. To make my case, I¡¯ll use Ukraine as an example. When I first visited Ukraine, it was a fascinating and eye-opening experience for me. But not everyone would have seen it that way¡ªsome visitors would have absolutely hated it and counted the days until they could return home. But for most Ukrainians, the conditions I described weren¡¯t shocking¡ªthey were simply normal. That was the life they were used to and had lived for as long as they could remember. When I visited, about a decade after the collapse of the Soviet Union, the country was going through an extremely rough period. I was told that many people weren¡¯t being paid on time by their employers, and that this was not unusual at all. Yet they still had to show up for work if they wanted to keep their jobs. Most of them did¡ªbecause they felt they had no other options and believed they¡¯d eventually be paid (and from what I understand, most of them were, eventually). Why weren¡¯t they paid on time? I was told it was simply because there was no money. But here¡¯s my point: despite all of this, they still managed to find joy. They still celebrated, laughed, and lived their lives as best they could. That¡¯s what we call resilience and perseverance. It¡¯s the same spirit Americans had during the Great Depression and the Second World War.***

question_title: (5) What is the importance of festivals in life? - Quora
answer_text: Festivals are a kind of ¡°first-order thinking¡± solution to our daily struggles¡ªa ¡°jugaad¡± (quick fix) for happiness. During festivals, people act as if all problems have disappeared. Everyone exchanges greetings, pretending to be happy, no matter their hardships. Important tasks are postponed with the phrase, ¡°Let¡¯s do it after Diwali.¡± Meanwhile, roads remain broken, unemployment rises, inequality deepens, corruption spreads, rivers get polluted, and farmers and laborers continue to suffer. Yet, we must smile¡ªbecause it¡¯s a festival, like popular slogan, "?????????? ?? ???? ??? ??"(smile you are in Lucknow). Festivals keep us busy, which can be good, but they also distract us from the real work that needs to be done. Festivals in India seem to have become show-off days for the rich. No festival passes without spending money¡ªsomething the rich do extravagantly¡ªwhile the poor watch this spectacle like an audience watching a drone show in a stadium. The festive vibe today feels incomplete without lavish spending. The rich, being financially capable, use these occasions to display their economic power, while the poor experience exclusion and a sense of being left out, lacking both money and material possessions. Festivals add color to the already beautiful lives of the wealthy, but for the poor, they often bring distress. For a family already struggling to make ends meet, their suffering deepens when they cannot afford even the basic festive essentials. A father knows the pain of seeing his children without new clothes or sweets, while a mother struggles to comfort them, saying, ¡°Next time, we¡¯ll buy everything.¡± I know how it feels¡ªwe spent every festival of my childhood watching others wear new clothes and burst firecrackers, and upon returning home, we faced a very different atmosphere¡ªa sad father and a mother doing everything she could to make her children happy. We are social beings, connected in every aspect of life. Not having something doesn¡¯t hurt until our neighbor has it. This is a universal truth. There¡¯s a beautiful English idiom, ¡°to keep up with the Joneses,¡± which describes the social pressure to maintain a certain status by acquiring the same or better things than those around us. It¡¯s not just about extravagant spending¡ªthere are also essential expenditures we must bear during every festival. India is a land of festivals, especially among Hindus, and they are an endless cycle: as soon as one ends, preparations for the next begin. Festivals are good for the market since they boost the economy. For thousands of years, festivals have contributed to economic growth, which is why shopkeepers eagerly await them. People are compelled to buy festival-related items, not only to ¡°keep up with the Joneses,¡± but also to fulfill religious obligations that few dare to question, even if they seem illogical. Social evils are deeply rooted in our society, but when linked with festivals, they often go unquestioned. If you have eyes in a society where everyone is blind, what use are they? No one will believe you when you say that color exists and the world is visible. Some people make the mistake of speaking the truth and end up isolated. So, if one uses logic, it¡¯s often better to keep it private. Yet many do the opposite¡ªthey know the truth but still go with the flow, masking superstitions with pseudo-scientific explanations and turning everything into a spectacle of wealth. During festivals, people follow every ritual to the smallest detail. Women, in particular, are more devoted, believing these rituals ward off misfortune. Whether it¡¯s Diwali, Holi, Onam, Lohri, or Chhath Puja, every tradition is followed earnestly. But I often wonder¡ªwhy are there so many festivals, and why were they created in the first place? The answer, I feel, is that they were designed to keep the human mind occupied and entertained. Over time, new rituals kept getting added to the basic ones¡ªlike firecrackers during Diwali¡ªand later, commercial interests expanded them further to boost markets. Every festival leaves behind a trail of waste¡ªDiwali with firecracker debris, Holi with scattered colors¡ªnone promote cleanliness or hygiene. People dump garbage and even ¡°sins¡± into the Ganga, and after cleansing others for centuries, the river itself has become polluted. Festivals are deeply tied to religion, and questioning them is often seen as questioning faith itself. Although we know that firecrackers were never part of Diwali originally¡ªthey were introduced only in the late 19th century¡ªfew dare to speak against them. Despite the health risks, especially in cities like Delhi already suffering from poor air quality, social and political fear prevents open criticism. question_title: (5) Why can¡¯t people just trust the science that there are 2 genders? - Quora
answer_text: Science says no such thing. The basics of what science says is: Social Construction: Gender roles, behaviors, and expectations are learned through socialization, not just biology, and differ by culture and era. Gender identity: A person's internal sense of being a man, woman, both, neither, or another gender, which may or may not align with the sex assigned at birth (cisgender vs. transgender). Gender expression: How someone outwardly presents their gender through clothing, mannerisms, and behaviors, which can be masculine, feminine, androgynous, or beyond. Beyond the binary: Gender isn't just male or female; it includes non-binary, genderfluid, agender, and other identities, reflecting a continuum rather than two fixed points. Impact: Gender influences how people see themselves, interact with others, and how power, resources, and opportunities are distributed in society. Religion, ideology and personal ignorance may say something else but all these three categories are quite the opposite of being scientific. Gender vs Sex: Sex: Refers to biological traits (chromosomes, anatomy, hormones) typically (commonly) categorized as male or female at birth. Gender: The social, cultural, and personal experience of identity and roles, distinct from biological sex. Not even biological sex is binary: There are plenty of naturally occurring biological atypical (not the common) variations in sexes among human. Chromosomal abnormalities in the sex chromosome - for example XXY boys, XYY boys, XXX Girls, X0 girls and so on. Maternal hormonal deficiencies or fetus insensibility to hormones - in some cases results in the development of dual genitalia (female and male) in the same fetus, in other cases resulting in severly underdeveloped genitalia (sometimes not even reconizable as male of female). None of these are of the typically binary male or female sex but either both sexes or not quite one or the other sex. Medically this category of "out of the binary sexes" is called intersex. Latest research says around 1¨C2% of the population have intersex treats. To sum it all up: Science says there is no such thing as only two genders. Science says no such thing as there are only two sexes. Please, stop taking your imagination and world view as science. Ignorance may be a bliss but it's certainly not productive.

question_title: (5) How far are we from achieving artificial general intelligence (AGI)? - Quora
answer_text: As of my last knowledge update in September 2021, it is difficult to provide a precise timeline for when we will achieve Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) because it is a complex and open-ended research problem. AGI refers to machines that possess general intelligence comparable to human intelligence, meaning they can understand, learn, and apply knowledge in a wide range of tasks and domains. At that time, there were various opinions within the AI research community regarding the timeline for achieving AGI. Some experts believed it could take several decades or more, while others were more cautious and acknowledged that it might be even longer or might never be fully realized. Since my last update, there have been significant developments in AI and machine learning, but AGI remains an elusive goal. Research in AI continues to progress, with advancements in areas such as deep learning, reinforcement learning, natural language processing, and robotics. However, these are still narrow or specialized AI systems designed for specific tasks, and they do not possess the broad general intelligence that characterizes AGI. It's important to note that predicting the timeline for AGI is highly speculative, and many technical, ethical, and societal challenges must be addressed along the way. Researchers are working on making AI systems more capable and adaptable, but achieving true AGI is a complex and multifaceted endeavor that may take many years, if not decades or more. For the most up-to-date information on the progress toward AGI, I recommend consulting recent publications, news articles, and the work of leading AI researchers and organizations. AGI's timeline is a topic of ongoing debate and discussion within the AI community, and it's subject to change based on new breakthroughs and insights. The greatest fear about AI is singularity (also called Artificial General Intelligence), a system capable of human-level thinking. According to some experts, singularity also implies machine consciousness. Regardless of whether it is conscious or not, such a machine could continuously improve itself and reach far beyond our capabilities. Even before artificial intelligence was a computer science research topic, science fiction writers like Asimov were concerned about this and were devising mechanisms (i.e. Asimov¡¯s Laws of Robotics) to ensure the benevolence of intelligent machines. For those who came to get quick answers: Will singularity ever happen? According to most AI experts, yes. When will the singularity happen? Before the end of the century. The consensus view was that it would take around 50 years in 2010s. After the advancements in Large Language Models (LLMs), a leading AI researcher, Hinton, updated his view and believes that it could take 20 years or less. The more nuanced answers are below. There have been several surveys and research of AI scientists asking about when such developments will take place. Understand the results of major surveys of AI researchers in 2 minutes We looked at the results of 5 surveys with around 1700 participants where researchers estimated when singularity would happen. In all cases, the majority of participants expected AI singularity before 2060. In the 2022 Expert Survey on Progress in AI, conducted with 738 experts who published at the 2021 NIPS and ICML conferences, AI experts estimate that there¡¯s a 50% chance that high-level machine intelligence will occur until 2059. Older surveys had similar conclusions. In 2009, 21 AI experts participating the in AGI-09 conference were surveyed. Experts believed AGI will occur around 2050, and plausibly sooner. You can see above their estimates regarding specific AI achievements: passing the Turing test, passing third grade, accomplishing Nobel worthy scientific breakthroughs and achieving superhuman intelligence. In 2012/2013, Vincent C. Muller, the president of the European Association for Cognitive Systems, and Nick Bostrom from the University of Oxford, who published over 200 articles on superintelligence and artificial general intelligence (AGI), conducted a survey of AI researchers. 550 participants answered the question: ¡°When is AGI likely to happen?¡± The answers are distributed as 10% of participants think that AGI is likely to happen by 2022 For 2040, the share is 50% 90% of participants think that AGI is likely to happen by 2075. Keep in mind that AI researchers were over-optimistic before Examples include: AI pioneer Herbert A. Simon in 1965: ¡°machines will be capable, within twenty years, of doing any work a man can do.¡± Japan¡¯s Fifth Generation Computer in 1980 had a ten-year timeline with goals like ¡°carrying on casual conversations¡± This historical experience contributes to most current scientists shying away from predicting AGI in bold time frames like 10-20 years. However, just because they are more conservative now doesn¡¯t mean that they are right this time around. Understand why reaching AGI seems inevitable to most experts These may seem like wild predictions, but they seem quite reasonable when you consider these facts: Human intelligence is fixed unless we somehow merge our cognitive capabilities with machines. Elon Musk¡¯s neural lace startup aims to do this but research on brain-computer interfaces is in the early stages. Machine intelligence depends on algorithms, processing power, and memory. Processing power and memory have been growing at an exponential rate. As for algorithms, until now we have been good at supplying machines with the necessary algorithms to use their processing power and memory effectively. Considering that our intelligence is fixed and machine intelligence is growing, it is only a matter of time before machines surpass us unless there¡¯s some hard limit to their intelligence. AGI is not possible because it is not possible to model the human brain Theoretically, it is possible to model any computational machine including the human brain with a relatively simple machine that can perform basic computations and has access to infinite memory and time. This is the Church-Turing hypothesis laid out in 1950. It is universally accepted. However as stated, it requires certain difficult conditions: infinite time and memory. And remember, you are not alone in this. Many are feeling the same ache, and together, you can find your way back to what truly matters.¡± --- Kian left the park that night with a lighter heart. question_title: (4) What is a generative AI? - Quora
answer_text: Generative AI refers to a subset of artificial intelligence that focuses on creating or generating new content, such as images, text, music, or even video, based on patterns and examples from existing data. Unlike traditional AI models that are designed for specific tasks, generative AI models have the ability to generate novel and original content that resembles the patterns observed in the training data. Generative AI works by utilizing complex algorithms and neural networks, typically based on deep learning architectures such as Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) or Variational Autoencoders (VAEs). These models learn from vast amounts of training data to understand and capture the underlying patterns, structures, and distributions present in the data. Generative AI models have been applied to various creative tasks, such as generating photorealistic images, composing music, creating natural language text, and even generating deepfake videos. These models have the ability to produce content that closely resembles the training data, but they can also introduce new and imaginative variations, making them valuable tools for artists, designers, and researchers.

answer_text: Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) are two terms that are often used interchangeably, but they are not the same thing. While they are both related to the field of computer science, they have distinct differences. In this article, we'll explore the difference between AI and ML and how they are used in real-world applications. Difference between Machine Learning and AI? AI refers to the simulation of human intelligence in machines that are programmed to perform tasks that would typically require human intelligence, such as decision-making, visual perception, and speech recognition. AI systems are designed to learn from experience, adapt to new situations, and improve their performance over time. On the other hand, ML is a subset of AI that refers to the use of algorithms and statistical models to enable computers to learn from data and improve their performance on a specific task. In other words, ML is a technique for creating AI systems. ML algorithms can be divided into two categories: supervised and unsupervised learning. In supervised learning, the algorithm is trained on a labeled dataset, where each data point is associated with a label or target variable. The algorithm learns to make predictions based on the input data and the associated labels. In unsupervised learning, the algorithm is trained on an unlabeled dataset, where there are no target variables or labels. The algorithm learns to identify patterns and relationships in the data without any pre-existing knowledge. Emotional connection: As people spend time together and get to know each other, they may develop a deep emotional connection. This can involve feeling understood and accepted by the other person, and feeling a sense of companionship and support. Similarities: People may be more likely to fall in love with someone who shares similar values, beliefs, interests, and goals. Proximity: Being around someone frequently can increase the likelihood of developing romantic feelings. This is known as the "mere exposure effect," which suggests that people are more likely to like and develop positive feelings towards things or people that they are familiar with. Chemistry: Some people believe that there is a certain "chemistry" or spark that exists between two people who are meant to be together. This can involve a strong physical attraction and an emotional connection. In conclusion, there are many factors that can contribute to the experience of falling in love, including physical attraction, emotional connection, similarities, proximity, and chemistry. question_title: (5) How does culture influence human behavior? - Quora
answer_text: Culture is a set of values, beliefs, norms, and customs that are shared by a group of people. Every culture is different and has its own unique way of looking at the world. This can lead to different types of behaviors that may be considered normal in one culture but strange or even wrong in another. For example, hugging and kissing in public might be perfectly acceptable in some cultures but considered quite taboo in others. In other words, our culture dictates what we consider acceptable or taboo behavior, which can influence our choices and actions. For example, in some cultures, it is acceptable to eat dog meat, while in others, it is considered repulsive. In addition, cultural differences can lead to misunderstandings and conflict. For instance, when two people from different cultures interact, they may have different ideas about what is considered polite behavior. This can lead to misunderstanding and conflict if they cannot effectively communicate with each other. Culture is influential because it helps to shape our identities. It allows us to belong to a group and feel like we have a shared purpose or mission. Culture can also provide us with a sense of stability and community in an ever-changing world. Additionally, culture can be a source of creativity and inspiration. When we are exposed to new ideas and perspectives, we can learn new ways of thinking and problem-solving. Finally, culture can be a source of strength during difficult times. When we feel disconnected from our culture, we may feel lost and alone. However, by reconnecting with our culture, we can find comfort and support.

question_title: (5) Is AI an existential threat to humanity? - Quora
answer_text: There is ongoing debate in the scientific and philosophical communities about whether or not artificial intelligence (AI) poses a threat to humanity. Some experts believe that AI has the potential to become an existential threat to humanity, while others argue that the risks are overstated or that it is too early to make such predictions. On one hand, some experts are concerned that as AI systems become more advanced, they could develop goals or values that conflict with those of humans. For example, an AI system designed to optimize a specific objective might take actions that are harmful to humans or the environment in pursuit of that objective, particularly if it has incomplete information or is poorly designed. In addition, some experts worry that AI systems could become too powerful for humans to control, potentially leading to unintended consequences or catastrophic outcomes. On the other hand, there are many experts who argue that AI can be designed in ways that prioritize human values and safety. They point out that many AI systems are already in use today in ways that are beneficial to society, such as in healthcare, transportation, and finance. They also argue that we can work to design AI systems that are transparent, ethical, and accountable to human oversight. Overall, while there are certainly risks associated with the development of AI, it is still too early to definitively say whether AI poses an existential threat to humanity. It is important for researchers, policymakers, and the public to engage in ongoing discussions and debates about the responsible development and use of AI in order to mitigate potential risks and ensure that AI is used in ways that benefit humanity. question_title: (4) What is a generative AI? - Quora
answer_text: Generative AI refers to artificial intelligence systems that have the ability to generate content, such as text, images, audio, or video, often in a creative and human-like manner. There are several types of generative AI models and techniques that have been developed. Some of the notable types of generative AI include: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs): GANs consist of two neural networks, a generator and a discriminator, that are trained together in a competitive process. The generator creates data, while the discriminator tries to distinguish between real and generated data. question_title: (5) What are the most common misconceptions about AI? - Quora
answer_text: There are several misconceptions about AI that often lead to confusion about its capabilities and limitations. One of the biggest myths is that AI is fully autonomous and can think like humans. In reality, AI operates based on algorithms and data; it does not possess consciousness, emotions, or true reasoning abilities. Another common misconception is that AI will soon replace all human jobs. While AI automates certain tasks, it is more likely to complement human work rather than completely replace it, creating new job opportunities in the process. Many people also believe that AI is infallible and unbiased. However, AI systems are only as good as the data they are trained on. If the training data contains biases, the AI model will reflect and even amplify them. Similarly, some assume that AI is universally applicable and can solve any problem, but AI works best in specific, well-defined tasks and often struggles with tasks requiring deep human intuition. Another misunderstanding is that AI is a recent invention. While modern AI has gained significant advancements due to increased computing power and data availability, AI concepts date back to the 1950s. Lastly, some people fear AI will become self-aware and take over the world, a scenario often popularized by sci-fi movies. In reality, today¡¯s AI is far from achieving general intelligence, and experts are still debating whether true artificial general intelligence (AGI) is even possible. Understanding these misconceptions helps in having a more realistic perspective on AI's capabilities, limitations, and its role in shaping the future.

question_title: (5) What are the most common misconceptions about AI? - Quora
answer_text: One of the most common misconceptions about AI is that it can be a net benefit to humanity. Above: Mark Zuckerberg, Sam Altman, Elon Musk, Sundar Pichai ¡ª four of the many AI-involved men paving the way towards a very dark future. There are generally two types of people who believe AI can be a net benefit to humanity: the technophile and the utopianist. The technophile is a person who loves and supports technological development no matter what. For him, science and technology play a vital role in his psychological constitution ¡ª they give him ¡°purpose¡±, excitement and/or temporary satisfaction. Naturally, it would take an invention such as the nuclear weapon ¡ª inarguably terrible ¡ª for such a person to even contemplate expressing strongly negative views against technology. In essence, the technophile is a true believer of technology, and it¡¯s therefore only natural that he welcomes AI. Above: Raymond Kurzweil ¡ª a perfect example of a technophile. The utopianist, on the other hand, is not a true believer of technology. He is usually a na?ve commoner in that he views AI as a ¡°redeemable¡± technology. The utopianist will with no hesitation state that the development and implementation of AI has some severe risks that ought to be taken seriously, but will later also point at all the ¡°good¡± AI can do. As a solution, he will invariably propose regulations ¡ª if only we regulate, we can enjoy the good whilst mitigating or even eliminating the bad. And this is the reason I call them ¡°utopianists¡±: they treat regulations as if they are some sort of magic wand that can protect and improve society indefinitely. In fact, history clearly shows that laws and regulations are never permanent and that they have a rather short lifespan. Moreover, it should be noted that regulations will only be enforced if they do not debilitate the competitive standing of the country/organization on the global stage. The US or China will not refrain from using the most potent aspects of AI because they can never be sure their rivals won¡¯t use them. In effect, this means that few heavy regulations will be put in place. The EU AI regulations are a good example of this ¡ª these were by and large token regulations which did not even address ¡°AI systems¡± in the military. Furthermore, even in the incredibly unlikely scenario where the regulations were devised perfectly and were permanent globally, that would still not mean that AI would benefit humanity. Why? Because AI is a fundamentally disempowering technology in that it is designed to reduce the masses to complete redundancy whilst empowering the elites. This might not be what many of the computer scientists that actively develop the technology would say, but everything points to this being true. History certainly supports such a conclusion; ever since the Industrial Revolution, every major technological breakthrough has resulted in an increasingly centralized society in which the elite¡¯s power has grown steadily in tandem with the gradual disempowerment of the masses. There is no reason to believe that AI, which is controlled by the elites, will result in a different outcome. As an example of how this might come to be, consider the following possible outcome. As AI develops, it will eventually become more capable than all humans. This will provide employers a superior alternative to human workers, paving the way for mass-unemployment. In fact, this process has already begun with companies such as Amazon and Duolingo already replacing workers with AI. Once a significant number of people have become unemployed, the pressure for ¡°Universal Basic Income¡± will become stronger ¡ª but one should not be so sure that this will be granted. Remember, at this point, AI will have developed to such an extent that people will be completely powerless against it and its masters. One should never forget that the only reason the elites consider the opinions and demands of the commoners is because not doing so may risk their position and even their lives. However, with controlled, advanced AI in the picture, everything changes. No longer do they need to listen to the masses as they have no power to enforce their demands. Given this, how could people force the elites to grant them UBI? Conversely, how would granting UBI to the unemployed masses benefit the now extremely powerful elite? The masses have by this point not only become redundant, they have also become harmful as they waste precious resources in a thoroughly exploited planet. Logically, it would be far more efficient to eradicate the masses rather than sustaining them through UBI, and thereby needlessly losing precious resources. What type of ¡°regulations¡± could stop this dreadful scenario? Forcing companies to employ humans? Again, this would debilitate their competitive standing vis-¨¢-vis their global rivals, potentially resulting in their demise. This alone makes it wholly unrealistic that such restrictive regulations would be put in place. Still, for the sake of dispelling the unfounded idea that AI can be a net benefit to humanity, let us pretend that somehow the most ideal regulations are put in place and that, after the mass-unemployment occurs, the elite, in their magnanimity, grants the masses UBI instead of seeking to eradicate them. A happily ever after? No ¡ª far from it. The immense power imbalance between the AI-steering elites and the masses will still remain, meaning that they would easily be able to enforce all sorts of unopposable, tyrannical measures such as unprecedented intrusive surveillance and genetic engineering. The masses would in this scenario essentially become domesticated animals with no freedom. I fail to see how this can be a net benefit to humanity. Above: Drone surveillance. As intrusive as this is, one can be sure that future surveillance methods will be even more so. Of course, throughout this post I have, for the sake of clarity, assumed that the elites will be able to maintain control over AI. Needless to say, this is not guaranteed. Several AI experts such as Geoffrey Hinton and Max Tegmark even claim that the risk of a rogue AI emerging and wiping us out is uncomfortably high. It would be difficult to argue that a rogue AI can be a net benefit to humanity. The plight of the environment should also be mentioned. AI will inevitably result in immense environmental degradation, regardless of outcome. The energy and water demands of this beast are simply gargantuan. For example, in 2022, AI accounted for 2% of global energy usage. By 2026, the International Energy Agency predicts that AI¡¯s electricity consumption will double, using about as much as Japan. It is safe to say that as AI develops, it will devour more resources and subsequently contribute to one environmental disaster after another. All in all, the more AI is developed and implemented, the more vulnerable and redundant people will become ¡ª regardless of whether ¡°proper¡± regulations are put in place. As such, I would strongly urge utopianists and people in general to move away from the na?ve idea that regulations will solve the threatening AI problem we face.

question_title: (5) Are people who declaw their cats cruel, or is it sometimes necessary? - Quora
answer_text: My response to the original question: Are people who declaw their cats cruel, or is it sometimes necessary? I used to do volunteer work at an animal hospital back when it was considered normal to have your cat declawed. I was 12 and the vet liked me so he let me watch and sometimes assist in the surgeries. Pretty cool for a 12 year old! I saw interesting and sad things like when a dog somehow got mixed up with a hay bailer and his paw was amputated. The doctor could only clean up the amputation and sew it up. Anyway, I witnessed many declawings. The cat was put under and the the doctor would press on the cats paw to extend the nails. He would then take the tool which was used to trim a dog's nails and snip off the claws just below where they started to grow. He would then apply a silver stick which would stop the bleeding and bandage them up. It would be like if your fingers were cut off just beyond the base of your nail. I know I wouldn't like that and it would make doing many things much more difficult. Around that time I adopted a 16 year old Siamese. She had been someone's breeding cat and was no longer able to have kittens. When she herself was a kitten her owner had her front paws declawed. (At the time they felt it was more humane to just get the front ones declawed than all 4. I guess they were on their way to figuring out the whole process was inhumane) The doctor who performed the declawing put the bandages on too tight and left on a farm call. question_title: (5) If humans evolved from apes, why are there still apes? - Quora
answer_text: Because NOT ALL APES EVOLVED INTO HUMANS. Some did, but most of them evolved into the different apes we share the world with. Those guys¡¯ ancestors lived in the forest, while our ancestors moved onto the savannah, a grassy plain. They lives a different lifestyle than our ancestors did, and didn't directly compete with us for food and territory (not until much later, anyway). I¡¯ve been hearing this question for years, and it's just as short-sighted and ignorant now as it was thirty years ago when I was asking it as a teenaged Lutheran. The unspoken assumption in this question is that, the instant a group of apes evolved into a human ancestor, the entire rest of the species either magically all died simultaneously, or magically all transformed into that human ancestor. That is simply not how evolution works. The group of stem apes that became our ancestors became reproductively isolated from the rest of its species¡ªmaybe the group crossed a river in the dry season and got stuck on the far side during the wet season, so they settled in and made a home there; or maybe they got chased out of their territory by a pack of wolves or other predator, or maybe it was something else entirely. We really have no way of knowing how it happened, only that it did happen. If it hadn't, we wouldn't be having this discussion, because we¡¯d be flinging poo at each other in the African rainforest. Either way, that group¡¯s genes were isolated from the rest of the species, so they accumulated different mutations until eventually, they had changed to the point where they couldn't have successfully bred with a member of the original species if they¡¯d wanted to. This also happened to the rest of the species¡ªtheir genes were isolated from the group that would eventually give rise to Homo sapiens, so THEY accumulated different mutations et cetera. Repeat this process over and over for about 7 million years, and you eventually get us, chimps and bonobos, orangutans, and gorillas. Note that this process happened in the case of each of the above: the line that became chimps and us split off from the reat of the apes (then split again 7 million years ago to make us and chimps and bonobos), the another group split off and became orangutans, and another group became gorillas.

question_title: (5) Why must all forms of science be ¡°Agnostic¡± by necessity? - Quora
answer_text: To answer this we need to look at what comes in to science and what comes out. On the input side, we have observations. Real tangible verifiable facts that we discern directly or indirectly through our senses. This doesn¡¯t mean our senses are reliable data measurement instruments. What it does mean is that we are ultimately on a fundamental level confined to our senses in order to access the real world. On the output side, we have hypotheses. Now at its birth, a hypothesis will only be an idea like any other inside the clouds of our minds. But the hypothesis if accurate is supposed to describe the natural world we can observe. If they can¡¯t do that, then it is not a valid hypothesis. That means we discard the hypotheses that don¡¯t work, and only keep those that do. But there is a caveat to this, which is that some hypotheses can explain the world no matter what world we observe. They are fundamentally immune to being disproven. That might sound compelling, but it means the reason it perseveres is not because it survived scrutiny. It¡¯s because it is imperveous to being proven false. It cannot be used to discern what kind of world we live in, because it is never proven false in any possible world. It can of course garner significant support for itself, but it is worth noting that if a hypothesis cannot be disproven, then we would expect it to only garner positive support once considerable data has been gathered. In other words, in order to qualify for scientific scrutiny, the hypothesis must present some opportunity where it could be disproven if false. This is the fundamental scaffolding of science. The things we associate with science, such as beakers with foaming liquids, blinking machines and enormous building-sized telescopes are actually a byproduct of this process more than basic necessities. The method is primordial to science. And we can see a pattern in my description. Input of science is observations of the natural world. Output is hypotheses about the natural world. This is because science is fundamentally trying to model the natural world. If supernatural agents that are fundamentally outside the natural world and fundamentally distinct from anything within it routinely intervenes with the universe, then science will not be able to access those agents and study them. We could gather data on these anamolies and propose hypotheses that fit more or less well with observations, but ultimately we would have to put a big red question marks on these issues indefinitely. And make no mistake, there are a lot of big red question marks in science today. Some of which will likely remain there for a considerable time, if not forever. That does not mean science will suddenly start attributing gods to resolve the questions but just keep looking for a naturalistic explanation. This might seem constraining, especially if it turns out we really do live in a world of gods and demons. But we have these constraints there for a reason. And that is to minimize the impact our personal biases have on what we believe about the world. Science when it comes to its bare bones is just a systematic method of not fooling yourself.

question_title: (5) What are the most important things to know about personal finance? - Quora
answer_text: There are a lot of terms thrown around in personal finance, but Net Worth and Cash Flow are arguably the most important. How do you know if you are building wealth? Net worth can tell you. How healthy is your financial wellbeing? That¡¯s what you can learn from Cash Flow. It¡¯s important to understand what these terms mean and how they relate to one another. Net Worth Tells you whether you are building wealth and how quickly. The formula: OWN-OWE = NET WORTH The current value of everything you own (cash, investments, cars, house, personal property) minus what you owe (credit card balances, loans, mortgages) equals your personal net worth. Net Worth can be negative (owe > own) or positive (own > owe), but the critical piece of information is how your net worth is changing over time. If your net worth is growing (becoming more positive) over time, that means you are building wealth. If it is negative (or declining), that may be okay temporarily if there is a legitimate reason (stock market is declining). But the key is to understand why it is moving in that direction and to have a plan to reverse course if the underlying reason is controllable. Cash Flow Tells you where your money is going and how well you are managing it. The formula: CASH IN ¨C CASH OUT = NET CASH FLOW All of your sources of income (paycheck, rental income, child support, tax refund) minus what you spend it on (expenses, debt payment, savings, tax payments) equals your personal cash flow. Unlike Net Worth, your cash flow should never be negative because that means that you are spending more than you are bringing in. That¡¯s unsustainable and the primary reason people get into debt or go bankrupt. But a large or growing cash surplus can also be problematic if you don¡¯t have a plan to put it to good use. Excess cash flows can be reallocated to saving, investing, paying down debt, or purchasing more assets ¨C all things that will increase your Net Worth. The relationship between Net Worth and Cash Flow Positive cash flows create opportunities to increase net worth through increased savings or investments. Negative or declining cash flows usually mean your net worth is also falling or stagnating, mainly because you will have to plug the gap by taking on more debt or tapping into your savings. When you make a financial decision, it¡¯s critical to take time to weigh how it will affect both of these metrics. It¡¯s important to track and manage net worth and cash flow. Luckily most financial apps allow for this. I do not recommend trying to track net worth or cash flow in an Excel worksheet. It's a lot easier to let an app do the math for you.

A philosopher and cognitive scientist whose thinking is rooted in evolutionary theory, he is known around the world for his rousing defense of atheism and his detailed analysis of how the physical structures of the brain give rise to consciousness and what some might call our souls. He coauthored a book with one of his former undergraduate students, Mathew Hurley, A06¡ª Inside Jokes: Using Humor to Reverse-Engineer the Mind . Dennett¡¯s first bestseller was Consciousness Explained (1991), which set the stage for a number of other works, the latest being From Bacteria to Bach and Back . ¡°His special focus is the creation of the human mind,¡± Joshua Rothman wrote in a 2017 profile in The New Yorker . ¡°Into his own, he has crammed nearly every related discipline: evolutionary biology, neuroscience, psychology, linguistics, artificial intelligence.¡± He wholeheartedly subscribes to Darwin¡¯s idea that all of human creation¡ªfrom Michelangelo¡¯s art to your own thoughts as you watch TV¡ªhas ¡°created itself, not in a miraculous, instantaneous whoosh, but slowly, slowly,¡± through natural selection. One of the so-called Four Horsemen of the New Atheism¡ªalong with Richard Dawkins, Sam Harris, and Christopher Hitchens¡ªDennett explored the idea of religion as a natural phenomenon in his 2007 book, Breaking the Spell. And we are very dangerous.¡± On the plus side, he doesn¡¯t think that¡¯s coming anytime soon, even within a half century. In person, Dennett is remarkably down to earth¡ªwith his white beard and hand-whittled walking stick, he looks like a gentleman farmer. question_title: (5) Why must all forms of science be ¡°Agnostic¡± by necessity? - Quora
answer_text: There might be more than one way to interpret the word ¡°Agnostic¡±, but generally speaking, the word is applied to people who are religious but who say that God is impossible to understand and that humans are simply incapable of grasping the true reality of God. In other words, they are religious people who simply say that we can never fully know God. Therefore the name a-gnostic (un-knowable). In that sense of the word, it is NOT true that science must be agnostic, because science does not deal with religion in any form. However, you probably mean ¡°un-biased¡± instead of ¡°agnostic¡±. In that sense, it would be true to say that science must be un-biased, without any preconceived ideas. Because being biased would potentially mislead scientists and produce biased results, because scientists might give preference to one side or the other. Science must be neutral and objective in its research, not swayed by personal opinions, emotions , or beliefs. That is why science has developed methods such as double-blind studies and experiments, where neither the researcher nor the object of study know the conditions of the test. For example, if scientists are examining a new medical pill and its effectiveness, they test it on a large group of patients. Some of the patients receive the real medicine, while others receive a sugary pill as a placebo. And neither the scientists nor the patients know who is getting which pill. This is to eliminate all bias, to remove any subjective elements, and remain totally objective in finding out if the pill really works or not. And yes, the word ¡°agnostic¡± could be applied here, not in a religious sense, but in the sense of simply ¡°not knowing¡± which pill is which. The general attitude of scientists should always be: ¡°I don¡¯t know this, but I am working trying to find out.¡± That is the correct scientific approach. The reverse, the un-scientific method that some people try to apply in some situations is to start with an assumption about what the end result should be, such as ¡°This must be true¡±, and then just try to find arguments to support the position. This would be backwards science, because it starts with a final result and then tries to find some steps that would lead us toward that result. Instead, real science starts with simply ¡°not knowing¡± and then working to find the answer and simply follow the evidence no matter where it might lead us. Any kind of bias, or preconceived idea, or wanting to find a certain end result we desire, would taint the whole process of discovery.

question_title: (5) How do I start working as a freelancer? - Quora
answer_text: How to start freelancing To start freelancing while you already have a full-time job, you¡¯ll have to consider the following steps: Define your business goals Before you start freelancing, you¡¯ll have to be honest with yourself, and answer an important question: Is freelancing just a side gig? Or do you plan to expand it to a full-time business? The answer to this question will determine your next steps, considering that you¡¯ll either aim to balance your full-time and freelance work, OR aim to work your way out of your current job to pursue a full-time freelance career. The answer to this question is your long-term goal. To pursue it, you¡¯ll have to set a number of short-term goals and answer questions such as: What niche will you specialize in? What services will you offer? What amount do you want to be earning on a monthly basis to decide to quit your full-time job (if applicable)? These are just some of the vital questions and short-term goals you need to work through to take your freelancing career off the ground. Find a perspective niche (and stick to it) No matter whether you¡¯re a graphic designer, copywriter, developer, or anything in between by vocation, it¡¯d be best if you were to specialize in a particular area of work: For example, If you¡¯re a content writer, don¡¯t aim to write about any topic under the sun, from Top 3 Ways to Prepare Your Garden for Spring to Taxation Laws in all 50 US States Explained. Sure, you may start by writing various topics, to find your ideal niche, but eventually, you should pick one, and stick to it. But, Cryptocurrency or Technology content writer always sound much better in your CV than General content writer. Moreover, they inspire more confidence in you on the part of the clients who¡¯ll always be looking for specific, and not general content. The same is true if you¡¯re a graphic designer: consider your level of experience your current pool of connections your natural inclinations to a particular design niche Then, make your pick ¡ª focus on delivering interface design for apps, creating new custom logos, devising layouts for books, or any other specific design work. Now, this doesn¡¯t mean you should downright refuse to work on anything else. But, you will be building your experience, skills, and reputation in one specific line of work, which will increase your likelihood of getting hired to do side gigs for reputable companies looking for experts in a particular niche.* *You should check with your employer on what¡¯s the company¡¯s policy of working on such side hustles. Perhaps your contract forbids you from accepting freelance work in your respectable niche, outside of the company. Identify target clients Just like you shouldn¡¯t aim to cover every niche in your industry, you shouldn¡¯t aim to cater to the needs of the entire industry¡¯s market. Small businesses, teams, remote workers, or even other freelancers may all require the same type of service you¡¯re looking to offer. But, you¡¯ll need to target one or two types of clients especially. Say you want to start a blog about everything related to working remotely. There are freelancers, teams, but also entire businesses working remotely, and they can serve as your starting point. But, just like with choosing a niche, specific is always better. Think about the age of your desired readers. Perhaps you¡¯re a Millennial, so you can write a blog about working remotely for Millennials? Think about the location. Perhaps you want to cover predominantly the US market? Think about the education level. Perhaps you want to cover newly independent remote workers, who¡¯re just starting out their careers? Think about income. Perhaps you¡¯re looking to write for people with a limited budget, but who want to try digital nomadism? Think about gender. Perhaps you want to predominantly target women freelancers? These are only some questions you should ask yourself, but they reveal a lot. For example, that you can write for fresh-out-of-college female Millennials from the US looking to start and cultivate a remote career while traveling abroad with a limited budget. This is specific enough to draw in the right crowd, but general enough not to alienate other remote workers. After all, you¡¯ll still mostly write about challenges, tips, and hacks of remote work, which will likely interest all remote workers. But, you¡¯ll get a more specific idea where and how to market your blog, and what kind of copy you should write for your Landing page and subsequent pages. Set your freelance rates Setting your freelance rates always seems like a challenging point, but it¡¯s a lot more straightforward when you list the necessary parameters that help determine your ideal (and realistic) pricing: Experience (if any) Education level Supply and demand for your services The prices in your industry Your location Once you have all this data, you¡¯ll need to calculate your hourly rate based on it ¡ª higher education, experience, and demand for your niche will mean you can set higher prices. If you¡¯re based in the US, you¡¯ll likely be able to command higher rates than if you¡¯re based in the Philippines. Of course, your living standards and expenses will be higher, so you¡¯ll also need to command higher rates. In any case, you shouldn¡¯t price yourself too high in relation to the listed parameters ¡ª because you¡¯ll become too expensive to clients when compared to the competition. But, even more importantly, you shouldn¡¯t sell yourself short either. After all, you¡¯ll need to think about covering your freelance expenses and making a profit. However, once you price your work too low, it¡¯ll be difficult to increase your prices later, even if you find that you need to. Create a website (and portfolio) Once you¡¯ve defined your business goals, found a niche, identified your target clients, and set your prices, you¡¯ll want to create an online presence. And, the best way to do so is by creating your own website with a portfolio showcasing your previous work, skills, and expertise. Creating a website for free through a website builder like Wix is fine, but you¡¯ll be better off if you were to buy a domain name from a hosting website. You¡¯ll get a unique name for your online presence and a customized email address, so you¡¯ll look much more credible and overall more professional to potential clients. Regardless of what your industry is, it may be best if you were to choose your own name for the domain, especially when you¡¯re mostly looking to showcase your portfolio. You¡¯ll stand out better, and it¡¯ll later be easier to switch to a different industry (or niche) if you find that you want to. Once you¡¯ve selected a host and domain name, you can install WordPress to your website, and choose the website¡¯s theme. Then, you can add a landing page describing your services, and prices, maybe even a separate page for a blog where you¡¯ll write about industry-related topics. Don¡¯t forget to optimize your website for search engines. Include the most common industry-related keywords in your copy, to help Google position you better, and clients find you easier. Most importantly, create a separate page just for your portfolio ¡ª depending on your industry, this can be: a video reel (if you¡¯re a video producer, 3D, or 2D animator¡­) a selection of your best photographs (if you¡¯re a photographer) an overview of your best articles (if you¡¯re a writer) Find your first client Your first client may contact you because of your personal website portfolio, but you should also actively pursue your first gig bearing in mind what employers look for. There are several ways you can do this: Get involved in your industry¡¯s community Join a forum catering to your industry, offer opinions on pressing issues and questions, and partake in discussions. Also, don¡¯t be afraid to ask questions yourself. If you see a wall mural, application, logo design, or any other industry-related work you like, contact the client who commissioned it and ask what he/she requested from the person who delivered the work. Ask how they found the freelancer they hired, and why they hired him/her. After all, clients can best tell you what they want from the professionals they hire. Learn how to pitch through email Knowing how to pitch your expertise and skills is as important as having said expertise and skills. And, sending cold emails to potential clients is a good way to start. So, identify potential clients in your industry (a simple Google search can suffice), and start crafting your emails: Personalize emails. Make sure you address the person in your email (avoid the popular ¡°To Whom It May Concern¡± phrasing). Make sure you pitch the email to therightperson. If you¡¯re pitching an online magazine to land a writing gig, make sure you send the pitch to the magazine¡¯s editor, and not the magazine¡¯s Art Director, or any other person unrelated to the field of writing. Create a thoughtful proposal. Do your research, understand what the company or website you¡¯re pitching to is looking for, and understand how your services tie into that. You¡¯ll probably need some practice with email pitching, but you¡¯ll get the answer to how efficient your emails are soon enough. If no one replies to you, you¡¯re likely doing something wrong and need to rethink your approach. Finding your first client is the most difficult, especially if you haven¡¯t yet made a name for yourself in your industry/niche. But, your first client (if he/she is satisfied with your work) can give you a referral to serve as your credibility among future clients. Look through freelance job platforms/websites You can go through general Freelance job platforms , but also those aimed at developers, designers, virtual assistants, writers, translators, etc Specifically, you can start with: Simply Hired, CareerBuilder, and FlexJobs (general) Github Jobs (development) If You Could Jobs (design) ProBlogger Job Board (writing) Then, work your way from there. Expand your network Once you¡¯ve landed your first client, you¡¯ll need to work on finding recurring clients. Perhaps your first client will become a recurring one. And, perhaps the referral you¡¯ve been given by said first client will inspire others to contact you and provide a steady stream of work. In any case, it¡¯s best that you expand your network ¡ª and here¡¯s where the famous Pareto Principle comes in handy. According to it, cultivating a good relationship with 20% of your clients will help you find 80% of new work through their referrals. Moreover, each new 20 referrals increase your chances of getting new projects by 80%. To expand your network, you can: partake in industry webinars attend events join Facebook groups and communities streamline your LinkedIn network send out invites to professionals in your field (or a field that often requires your services) Also, don¡¯t be shy about asking people you know in person (not just existing clients, but also your friends and family) to introduce you to new people. After all, you never know where you¡¯ll land your next gig, and it might even be in the local pub where the people from the neighboring marketing agency like to hang out. Balance your full-time job with your part-time freelancing side gigs All this talk about freelancing almost made you forget about your full-time job, didn¡¯t it? Well, it shouldn¡¯t. If you¡¯re working both full-time and on side freelance gigs, it¡¯s usually your full-time position that¡¯s covering your taxes, healthcare, retirement fund, and other subsequent expenses, most likely your bills too. So, it should remain a priority when compared to a string of part-time jobs. Make sure you keep in mind your deadlines, both at your full-time position and on your freelance projects ¡ª define your priorities, and make a schedule you¡¯ll stick to. If a fun freelance project overlaps with an important and urgent deadline at the office, you may want to pass on the opportunity. In such cases, always make sure you take care of your health, and leave sufficient time for meals, sleep, exercise, and leisure time with friends and family. On the other hand, if you¡¯re looking to become a full-time freelancer, then you should provide an answer to the previously mentioned question: What amount do you want to be earning on a monthly basis to decide to quit your full-time job? Your best bet is to pick a number that covers your current bills and the equipment you need for work, but also leaves enough for you to pay self-employment taxes and cover other expenses.

question_title: (4) How does ChatGpt work? - Quora
answer_text: At the most basic, easy-to-understand, and digest level, ChatGPT and other GPTs (Generative Pre-trained Transformers) work by simply guessing what the next word in the sentence should be. ChatGPT¡¯s job isn¡¯t to be correct or not lie; its basic job is to complete a sentence that sounds ¡°human enough.¡± ChatGPT does not understand what it is saying, or looking to make sense of what it has written down. ChatGPT does this by taking in a very large data set (basically all of the internet) and analyzing how sentences are formed from this data. It is then tasked with forming sentences of its own using this set. This starts the training portion of the model, where humans are required to tell it if its outputs are good or bad. A human would train it that ¡°dog over family toy brought¡± is not a sentence that makes sense and ¡®punish¡¯ it, and then reward the model when it creates a sentence such as ¡°the dog brought the toy to its family.¡± The model did not learn what this sentence means, but it now knows that this is how to make a sentence and be rewarded by a human for it, so it keeps trying to replicate this reward repeatedly. After it has been trained, then we can look at fine-tuning it as we are now in order to make it not just look at if what it is saying is literate, but also checking to make sure that it is telling us something truthful/accurate. At its very basic level, we are training it how we learn as humans. We start with babbling as babies, then moving to words, then putting words together, and finally understanding the deeper meaning of words and context completely. This is how ChatGPT works at a very basic, easy-to-understand level.

Opposite to the traditional focus of psychology and psychotherapy in the last decades, Positive Psychology studies the people who are happy, healthy and live a flourishing life. Without making to much of a detour, we can hence say that these key elements ¡°guarantee¡± a sane mental health. Here they are: (P)ositive emotions: People who are living a fulfilling life experience (a decent amount of) positive emotions but also actively cultivate emotions such as joy, gratitude, hope, love, satisfaction¡­ This active state of looking for experiences that provide positive emotions already increases well-being. (E)ngagement: Engagement is better known as ¡°Flow¡±. Experiencing the state of Flow - state we reach in activities where we feel deeply engaged, absorbed, where we loose track of time and of the external world - increases happiness and fulfillment. Such activities are defined by a balance between skills and challenges, clear goals, immediate feedback, a strong sense of control and an intrinsic motivation in the activity itself. (R)elationships: Building and maintaining healthy, positive, supportive and meaningful social relationships is another key to a happy life. We - Humans - are social animals by definition. We need to feel connected to others to maintain our mental health. Those relationships could be with family, friends, members of our community, etc. And I¡¯ll add that the same type of relationship to the Self is as important as the social ones! (M)eaning: Finding purpose and meaning to this life is another essential part of achieving a state of happiness and healthy stable mental state. Finding goals that support and align with our core values is crucial for this as much as these goals have to contribute to the greater good or to a larger purpose. (A)ccomplishment: Fostering a sense of accomplishment by pursuing and achieving goals that are meaningful, both in the short-term and long-term provides a sense of competence and increases well-being. Why be content with an absence of mental illness when you can shift the focus on building positive mental health and overall life satisfaction? The PERMA model gives insights on how to achieve this. Extend to New Markets There¡¯s no question that franchising gives you a chance to increase your customer base. Measure What Works and Refine as You Go While there are a variety of strategies you can use to grow your small business, it¡¯s important you measure what¡¯s working.
